title: Heterogeneous SLO-driven topology routing with soft-evacuation circuit brakes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent customer latency SLO violations when a single region experiences degraded GPU availability or transient network egress issues. Existing steering uses single-threshold geo-pinning and hard failover which either over-evacuates traffic or causes increased tail latency during flapping. Goal: Implement a topology-aware routing layer that applies heterogeneous SLO profiles per customer/route, uses latency + capacity signals to steer requests, and applies soft-evacuation circuit brakes (tokenized shedding with timed grace) instead of immediate hard failover. Non-goals: full autoscaler changes or model weight adjustments; this ticket focuses on request director policy and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy can express per-route SLO intent (p50/p90/p99 latency targets and throughput minima) as metadata
Routing engine uses a combined score (latency headroom, enqueue depth, GPU utilization) to compute per-region steering weights and exposes debug traces
Soft-evacuation circuit brake triggers when composite score crosses threshold for 30s and begins draining at a configurable rate (default 20%/min) instead of instant 100% ejection
Canary rollout: 5% of traffic to experimental policy for 48h with telemetry demonstrating reduced oscillation vs hard-failover in synthetic failure tests
Dashboards show SLO compliance delta pre/post and incidents with annotated rollback points
Runbook updated with playbook for manual override and rollback; team signoff from SRE and Runtime owners
design_decisions: Composite score: normalized 0..1 combining 95th latency headroom, region available token fraction (capacity), and KV cache hit degradation metric
Score weighting defaults: latency: 0.6, capacity: 0.3, cache: 0.1 but configurable per-customer via route metadata
Circuit brake design: two-phase soft-evacuation (drain fraction then incremental reduction) with cool-down to prevent thrash
Use existing token-bucket admission control as the shedding primitive; tokenized shed increments will be billed as dropped but logged with reason codes
Routing decisions are computed centrally in the request director and pushed as immutable hints to local edge proxies to minimize control-plane RT dependency
Fallback hierarchy: (1) local-weight-adjusted steering, (2) regional pinning respect for high-sensitivity customers, (3) last-resort global failforward to cheapest-compatible model variant
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + integration harness for synthetic region degradation (Feb 1 - Feb 5)
Phase 1: Internal canary on staging with 5% traffic (Feb 6 - Feb 10)
Phase 2: Gradual production canary 5% -> 20% over 48h if no regressions (Feb 11 - Feb 13)
Phase 3: 100% policy switch and monitor for 72h, revert on >2x SLO violations or >10% overall error delta (Feb 14)
Postmortem: Assess oscillation incidents and refine thresholds (within 2 weeks of full rollout)
monitoring_queries: Composite score histogram by region: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(region_composite_score_bucket[5m]))
Evacuation drain rate: gauge(region_traffic_fraction) compared to baseline_pre_rollout

notes: Trade-offs: centralized scoring simplifies consistent decisions but requires edge fallback heuristics to tolerate control-plane blips.
We choose soft-evacuation to reduce customer-visible oscillation; however it may temporarily increase p90 for some traffic slices while the drain completes.
Future follow-ups: expose per-customer SLA templates, integrate with Optimize to recommend thresholds, and evaluate coupling with autoscaler signals for proactive capacity pre-warming.
